cases.name: shell
cases.finding: Exact installed production desktop displayed its home and project views on private authenticated X11.

cases.name: process
cases.finding: Actual project install/start/explicit stop; owned listeners revoked, stale-scope stop rejected and owned descendants settled.

cases.name: protocol
cases.finding: Installed CLI exchanged actual scoped envelopes, accepted/rejected commands and current project views.

cases.name: preview
cases.finding: Actual production WebKit renders, increments, closes/reopens, survives deliberate fixture JS error; explicit Stop removes its window.

cases.name: interrupted-update
cases.finding: Actual Linux payload installation interrupted at pending, verified, published and activated boundaries; previous version retained.

cases.name: runtime-path-preservation
cases.finding: Installer writes only to disposable installation; original profile, tuned executables and active supervisor hashes preserved; current native recovery performs no authority/runtime transition.

cases.name: crash-startup
cases.finding: Actual current production desktop was killed and relaunched; both home screenshots were reviewed and identical.

cases.name: unknown-pending-operation
cases.finding: Each interrupted installation retains its pending receipt and refuses an unknown retry without treating it as completed.

cases.name: rollback-archive
cases.finding: Actual quiescent native archive restored after deliberate database corruption. Corrupt startup refused, corrupt bytes retained, installed CLI reopened and every original artifact verified. Production authority was not transferred.

scope: Linux x86_64 local tar candidate, actual installed desktop/CLI plus the current source-bound native archive helper. Scripted model fixtures for UI; recovery archive is from the actual live endurance workload. No Windows/macOS, signing, model-quality, full-duration or formal performance pass implied.
limitations: Private authenticated Xvfb and software rendering; user display is not controlled.
Runtime compatibility applies only to preserved Linux builds.
A passed recovery scenario inside a quality-failed duration is usable for its explicit platform behavior; it does not rescue the duration quality result.
Historical failed GUI driver attempts remain referenced by linux-installed-current.json.
Package rollback readability is distinct from production authority rollback; the production native owner is preserved.
